patterns.notProof: Patterns aren't proof of cause. Share them with your care team.
patterns.pat01Need: Patterns appear after {days} days of mood logs
patterns.pat02Need: Needs {days} days with a BM and {days} without, each with a mood log
patterns.pat03Need: Needs {days} logged days before and after the change
patterns.pat03Headline: Mood averaged {after}, {direction} from {before} in the {days} days before
patterns.pat03Meta: {days} days before and {days} days after · BMs a day {bmBefore} → {bmAfter} · behaviors {behBefore} → {behAfter}
patterns.pat03How: We averaged {name}'s daily mood for the {days} days before the change and the {days} days starting on it ({beforeDays} and {afterDays} days with mood logs), and counted BMs and notable behaviors in the same windows. Both sides need at least {min} logged days.
patterns.pat01Headline: {block} is usually the hardest part of the day
patterns.pat01How: We grouped {count} mood logs from {days} days into 3-hour blocks, using the time where each was logged, and averaged each block. The lowest average is called out. This needs {minDays} days and {minLogs} mood logs.
patterns.pat02Headline: On days with no BM, mood averaged {without}, compared with {with} on days with one
patterns.pat02Meta: {without} days without a BM, {with} days with
patterns.pat02How: For the last {days} days we split days by whether a BM was logged and compared the average daily mood. It's shown when the gap is at least {gap} points and each group has {min} or more days.
patterns.noDifference: No clear difference in mood between days with and without a BM ({with} and {without}).
patterns.footer: Patterns describe what was logged. They aren't a diagnosis or advice.
patterns.pat04Need: Needs one activity logged {times} times with a mood log in the 2 hours after
patterns.pat04Headline: Mood after {activity} averaged {avg}, compared with {overall} overall
patterns.pat04How: For each activity we averaged the mood logged in the {hours} hours after it ended, counting each time once, and compared that with the average of all mood logs. An activity needs {min} times with a mood log afterwards ({checked, plural, one {# activity had} other {# activities had}} enough). It's shown when it's at least {lift} points above the overall average.
patterns.pat04None: No activity stood out: mood after each one was less than {lift} points above the overall average ({overall}).
patterns.pat04NoneMeta: {last} · {checked, plural, one {# activity} other {# activities}} with enough logs
patterns.pat05Need: Needs {weeks} weeks of mood logs on every day of the week
patterns.pat05Headline: {hardest} is usually the hardest day ({hardestAvg}), {best} the best ({bestAvg})
patterns.pat05How: We averaged each day's mood (a day-level rating counts when there is one) and grouped the days by weekday. Every weekday needs {weeks} logged days. It's shown when the best and hardest days are at least {gap} points apart.
patterns.pat05None: Mood was about the same on every day of the week ({low} to {high}).
patterns.pat06Need: Needs {days} low-mood days and {days} other days, each with a meal or snack portion
patterns.pat06Headline: On low-mood days, {name} ate about {low}% of meals and snacks, compared with {other}% on other days
patterns.pat06How: For the last {days} days we averaged the portion eaten at meals and snacks each day, then compared days whose average mood was {mood} or lower with the rest. Each group needs {min} days. It's shown when the gap is at least {gap} percentage points.
patterns.pat06None: No clear difference in how much was eaten on low-mood days ({low}%) and other days ({other}%).
patterns.pat07Headline: {block} is when it's given most often
patterns.pat07HeadlineReason: {block} is when it's given most often, usually for {reason}
patterns.pat07How: We grouped as-needed doses that were given, fully or partly, into 3-hour blocks by the time they were logged, and counted the reasons. This needs {min} doses.
